comment: Offline and low-connectivity operation for the PHSP is classified 'Recommended' while FHIR-based integration, terminology subscription, and audit logging are 'Required'. For archipelagic, disaster-prone, devolved contexts this polarity is inverted: surveillance infrastructure must function precisely when infrastructure fails. Post-Haiyan assessments in the Philippines documented suspension of routine ESU surveillance, with roughly seven weeks to restore reporting in Leyte; operational resilience in practice meant paper and improvised channels. A platform 'designed to manage' public health emergencies (the requirement's own wording) cannot treat emergency operating conditions as optional.

public.suggestedRevision: Reclassify req. 21 from Recommended to Required. Specify a minimum offline floor: store-and-forward case capture, SMS-compatible notification of immediately notifiable events, and reconciliation rules on synchronisation, with conflict handling for case records edited offline at multiple sites.
